correctness.rationale: Odd characteristic: symmetric trace pairing and quadratic Gauss sums give squared multiplier q^{-r} for rank-r dual matrix; count nonsingular symmetric quotient forms by orthogonal group orders. Characteristic two: polar alternating rank 2r; a quadratic character vanishes unless its restriction to the polar radical is zero, with q^{2r} refinements per form and squared multiplier q^{-2r}; GL/Sp orbit counts yield exact multiplicity. Plancherel proves each time-dependent chi-square sum (with even formula only for t>=1 and separate t=0). Gaussian binomial dominated convergence gives both fixed-offset profiles. Upper TV follows chi-square, lower TV follows rank<=t and a union bound for uniform symmetric kernel planes. Finite direct convolution and complete small-field Fourier checks passed; these are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: Bounded statement-level comparison: Schmidt 2014/2018 give general association-scheme eigenmatrices for quadratic/symmetric forms, Fulman–Goldstein supply symmetric rank multiplicities, and Pak–Vu develop scalar-randomized geometric-walk cutoff machinery. None of their inspected specific theorem statements directly gives this unscaled Gram walk’s characteristic-split exact time-dependent chi-square sums, fixed-offset limiting series and both sides of the n-step total-variation cutoff. The result is not a minor special case of a located stronger cutoff/profile theorem, although classical ingredients make implied-priority a genuine risk.
residual_risks: The exact chi-square formula combines classical Fourier eigenmatrices and classical rank counts, potentially an implicit historical corollary; the reported priority conclusion is bounded.
No exhaustive literature search or independent specialist audit; an equivalent finite-field Wishart mixing law could exist under another terminology.
The fixed-offset series are not claimed as total-variation profiles.

value.rationale: The precise number of independent outer-product observations needed for near-uniformity of a sample Gram matrix is a structural matrix-sampling and Fourier-mixing question. The result gives all-time exact divergence, a bounded-window sharp mixing cutoff and explicit, nontrivially different characteristic-dependent chi-square profiles; these apply for every fixed prime-power alphabet and arbitrarily large dimension and are not a numerical table.
